items.t: Siemens Sees Poland’s Defense Buildup Driving Automation Demand
items.d: Siemens AG is betting Poland’s surge in defense and infrastructure investment will boost demand for industrial automation and digital technology as the German engineering group positions itself to capture a lucrative slice of the country’s spending boom.
items.fullText: Exclusive Technology Exclusive Siemens Sees Poland’s Defense Buildup Driving Automation Demand Facebook X LinkedIn Email Link Gift Facebook X LinkedIn Email Link Gift Gift this article Contact us: Provide news feedback or report an error Confidential tip? Send a tip to our reporters Site feedback: Take our Survey New Window Facebook X LinkedIn Email Link Gift By Agnieszka Barteczko October 13, 2026 at 11:18 AM UTC Bookmark Save Takeaways by Bloomberg AI Siemens AG is betting Poland’s surge in defense and infrastructure investment will boost demand for industrial automation and digital technology as the German engineering group positions itself to capture a lucrative slice of the country’s spending boom. Poland has secured as much as 43.7 billion euros ($49 billion) under the European Union’s SAFE defense-loan program, making it the bloc’s biggest beneficiary. Warsaw is deploying the funds to inject significant capital into its domestic defense industrial base as it responds to the security threat posed by neighboring Russia.

items.t: Orbital Data Centers Risk Becoming Military Targets in Space
items.d: Orbital data centers chasing unlimited solar power and boundless real estate increase the risk of potentially catastrophic conflict in space — just as militaries worldwide embrace artificial intelligence and see computing facilities as critical infrastructure.
items.fullText: Technology Orbital Data Centers Risk Becoming Military Targets in Space Facebook X LinkedIn Email Link Gift Facebook X LinkedIn Email Link Gift Gift this article Contact us: Provide news feedback or report an error Confidential tip? Send a tip to our reporters Site feedback: Take our Survey New Window Facebook X LinkedIn Email Link Gift By Gerry Doyle and Sana Pashankar October 13, 2026 at 9:12 AM UTC Bookmark Save Takeaways by Bloomberg AI Orbital data centers chasing unlimited solar power and boundless real estate increase the risk of potentially catastrophic conflict in space — just as militaries worldwide embrace artificial intelligence and see computing facilities as critical infrastructure. On the ground, government server farms are highly protected and can be buried to make them more resilient to attack. Iranian airstrikes targeted data centers across the Middle East, and Ukrainian attacks in recent days destroyed several in Russia, highlighting their perceived value.

items.t: 'HBM의 아버지' 김정호 KAIST 교수, 대전 과학기술혁신대상 수상
items.fullText: 테크 한경 PREMIUM9 AI를 넘어서는 성공투자 구독하기 AI 추천 뉴스 AI 추천 뉴스 팝업 닫기 'HBM의 아버지' 김정호 KAIST 교수, 대전 과학기술혁신대상 수상 입력 2026.10.13 15:18 수정 2026.10.13 18:30 지면 A29 기사 스크랩 기사 스크랩 댓글 댓글 기사 공유 공유 글자크기 조절 글자크기 프린트 프린트 정지은 기자 구독하기 구글 검색 선호 출처로 추가 Google 검색에서 한국경제 기사를 더 자주 볼 수 있습니다. ‘고대역폭메모리(HBM)의 아버지’로 불리는 김정호 KAIST 전기및전자공학부 교수(사진)가 대전광역시 개발위원회로부터 과학기술혁신대상을 받는다. 대전광역시 개발위원회는 올해 과학기술혁신대상 수상자로 김 교수를 선정했다고 13일 밝혔다. 개발위원회 측은 “김 교수는 한국이 인공지능(AI) 반도체 분야에서 세계적 경쟁력을 확보하는 데 기여한 공로가 크다”고 평가했다. 김 교수는 지난 30년간 HBM·고대역폭 플래시(HBF)·고대역폭 S램(HBS) 등 차세대 메모리 반도체 분야를 연구하며 기술을 개발했다. 특히 HBM의 핵심 개념과 기본 구조를 제안하고, 2009년 개발 과정에서 핵심 설계와 기술 검증에 참여했다. SK하이닉스가 2013년 12월 세계 최초로 HBM을 상용화하는 과정에도 참여했다. 시상식은 오는 15일 대전 롯데시티호텔에서 열린다. 정지은 기자 jeong@hankyung.com 좋아요 싫어요 후속기사 원해요 ⓒ 한경닷컴, 무단전재 및 재배포 금지 한국경제 구독신청 한경 프리미엄9 구독신청 정지은 기자 한국경제신문 산업부에서 전자업계를 담당하고 있습니다. 제보 메일 환영합니다. items.fullText: From Earth to Orbit, France’s Ecosystem Delivers Agentic Computing at Scale With NVIDIA French companies are putting NVIDIA infrastructure and open models to work across all industries, from satellites in orbit to cosmetics in corner stores. October 12, 2026 by Nat Ives 0 Comments Share Share This Article X Facebook LinkedIn Copy link Link copied! Companies in France are deploying agentic computing across industries spanning space, financial services, the public sector and scientific research, demonstrating how the country’s ecosystem has moved from ambition to application. France’s progress sits on deliberate groundwork. The AI Action Summit in February 2025 and Choose France Summits in 2025 and 2026 anchored major compute commitments on French soil. What the ecosystem has built since then spans the full stack. Read All NVIDIA in Europe Announcements Sovereign AI Infrastructure France-based companies are expanding agentic infrastructure on NVIDIA technology. Bull is extending its European AI server production to NVIDIA Vera Rubin Ultra NVL72 systems, planned for 2028, with trays produced in Europe and rack integration at its Angers factory — inaugurated Friday, Oct. 2. Altair-1, the first satellite in a $1 billion, 50-satellite constellation with on-board autonomous capabilities, launched this month and has successfully reached orbit. Integrated by Loft Orbital and built in Abu Dhabi by Orbitworks , a joint venture between Loft Orbital and Marlan Space , the satellite is flying NVIDIA Jetson AGX Orin edge modules, running Mistral’s models, for real-time Earth observation and autonomous operations in orbit. Open Models NVIDIA Nemotron open models are in production across French organizations that require sovereign, trustworthy data. LINAGORA and Docaposte have secured the CANUT framework agreement , making Twake.ai, built on NVIDIA Nemotron, the sole referenced sovereign digital workplace for more than 2,500 French public organizations. Elon Musk’s growing SpaceX empire sends AT&T, Verizon and T-Mobile shares plunging
items.d: Elon Musk’s plan for SpaceX to become a major mobile carrier sent shares of AT&T, Verizon and T-Mobile plunging and wiped out over $50 billion before lunch.
items.fullText: Corporations Elon Musk’s growing SpaceX empire sends AT&T, Verizon and T-Mobile shares plunging The company announced plans to “become a major mobile carrier in the U.S.” in part by buying spectrum and deploying satellites for its Starlink service. Listen to this article with a free profile 00:00 00:00 Starlink's mobile internet business is the single biggest money maker for Elon Musk's flagship company, SpaceX. Finn Gomez / Getty Share Add NBC News to Google Oct. 9, 2026, 1:55 PM EDT / Updated Oct. 9, 2026, 4:26 PM EDT By Steve Kopack Elon Musk’s plan for SpaceX to “become a major mobile carrier in the U.S.” sent shares of the nation’s big three wireless carriers sliding by double digits Friday, wiping out more than $50 billion in market value before lunch. “Once we receive final FCC approval, Starlink Mobile will deploy a flexible architecture combining our satellite-to-mobile constellation in space with an advanced terrestrial deployment that can seamlessly connect devices everywhere,” the company said late Thursday. It also announced that the Federal Communications Commission had approved the launch of 15,000 new satellites, also under Starlink Mobile, which is a subsidiary of SpaceX. Shares of AT&T fell 9.8%, Verizon dropped 8.7%, while T-Mobile US plunged 13.3%. For Verizon, today’s performance was its worst-one day drop since 2002. It was T-Mobile’s worst day since 2011. Shares of Charter and of Comcast, the parent company of NBC News, also fell Friday. Both companies sell wireless services under their own brands using Verizon’s infrastructure. Musk’s empire expands The announcement from SpaceX marked Musk’s latest step to expand his global tech empire. The world’s richest man and its first-ever trillionaire , Musk’s net worth as of Thursday was about $990 billion. In new Elon Musk documentary, his lieutenants are the most damning voices
items.d: ‘Musk,’ the new film from Alex Gibney, features interviews with more than the usual critics of the Tesla and SpaceX CEO.
items.fullText: ANALYSIS Elon Musk Elon Musk In new Elon Musk documentary, his lieutenants are the most damning voices “Musk,” the new film from Alex Gibney, features interviews with more than the usual critics of the Tesla and SpaceX CEO. Listen to this article with a free profile 00:00 00:00 SpaceX CEO Elon Musk in Washington on Sept. 29. Kent Nishimura / AFP via Getty Share Add NBC News to Google Oct. 9, 2026, 5:00 AM EDT By David Ingram SAN RAFAEL, Calif. — It’s easy to find people with bad things to say about tech magnate Elon Musk, and plenty of those people show up in “Musk,” a new documentary about his rise to political and corporate power. What’s more surprising in the film are the unflattering statements by some of his own employees, including ones who still work for him. Some of the harshest scenes in the film, which opens Friday in Los Angeles and New York, are ones in which Musk’s lieutenants were recorded on video or in audio as they wielded power on his behalf or discussed what they had already done for him. Warning: This article includes spoilers for the documentary “Musk.” There are clips of Ashok Elluswamy, a high-ranking Tesla engineer, acknowledging in a videotaped deposition that an infamous hype video he helped put together in 2016 about the company’s self-driving capabilities was not an accurate representation of Tesla’s technology at the time. There are also audio snippets from Jared Birchall, who handles Musk’s personal matters. He is heard on a recording of a phone call with online influencer Ashley St. Clair, shortly after she had given birth to a child she and Musk conceived, in which he plays hardball on child support arrangements. Both incidents were documented in the media: Reuters reported in 2023 on the transcript of Elluswamy’s deposition , and The Wall Street Journal reported last year on Birchall’s phone call with St. Clair.
